subject: Next steps: Hosted API evaluation and quickstart (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acmehealth.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Hosted API evaluation and quickstart (Acme Health)

Hi Emily / Carlos,

Thanks again for your time today — enjoy the quick recap and proposed next steps. Great discussion on your use case (clinical note summarization + HIPAA-adjacent PII detection) and the priority to get a low-friction integration that preserves patient data controls.

Recap (short):
- Recommendation: Start with Hosted API for fast time-to-value (no infra, quick API keys + console access).
- Why Hosted first: fastest onboarding for your engineers, ability to evaluate latency/cost on real traffic, and then move to Dedicated or Private if you need guaranteed capacity or on-prem data residency.
- Key ask from your side: sample payload (anonymized) and a list of peak concurrent requests / expected tokens per request so we can size limits for the eval.

Hosted API quickstart (what you get):
- Sandbox API key + console invite (I’ll provision this once you confirm the primary testing user).
- Default rate limits for evaluation: 120 requests/minute and 60,000 tokens/minute per API key. If you expect higher throughput during the POC we can request a temporary bump.
- Trial credit: 1M tokens of trial credit applied to the Acme eval account.
- Endpoints: text-generation (POST /v1/generate), chat (POST /v1/chat), and embeddings (POST /v1/embeddings).

Attachments: I attached the Redwood quickstart guide and the recording from today’s demo.

Next steps I propose:
1) Share the testing contact (name + email) so I can invite them to the console and issue the sandbox key.
2) Emily/Carlos share a small representative payload and peak throughput expectations (token/request and RPS).
3) Schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review initial logs and tune rate limits and batching (I’m available Tue 4/14 10–12 PT or Wed 4/15 2–4 PT).

If you prefer, we can also scope a short Dedicated pilot in parallel — I can loop in our solutions engineer to propose reserved capacity and cost estimate. But starting with Hosted will get you results fastest.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosted API evaluation and quickstart (Acme Health)

Ben — thanks for the recap and for the guide/recording. A few quick questions from the engineering and security teams: 

1) Rate limits — our workload is bursty. Peak could be ~400 req/min with ~8–12k tokens per request during nightly batch windows. Can Hosted hit that for a short POC or do we need Dedicated?
2) Data residency & logs — we need to understand where request logs and any persisted artifacts live and retention window for audit.
3) Sandbox API key — can we get a sandbox key scoped to a dev project (non-prod) and separate from production keys?

We’d like to start this week if possible. Also if there are any extra compliance docs (SOC2 summary, data processing agreement) you can share that would speed our internal review.

Appreciate it —
Emily Torres
Director, Data Engineering | Acme Health
emily.torres@acmehealth.com

Hi Emily — great questions. Quick answers below and a proposed temporary configuration for your POC.

1) Rate limits (Hosted):
- Default: 120 req/min and 60,000 tokens/min per API key (sized for typical dev/test workloads).
- POC bump: We can request a temporary evaluation increase to 600 req/min and 300,000 tokens/min for 14 days (requires sign-off from SRE and applied to your sandbox key). If you need more than that we would suggest a short Dedicated pilot.

2) Data residency & logs:
- Hosted US region is standard for your account by default. Production workloads can be pinned to an EU region if needed — ask me and we’ll create an EU tenant.
- Request logs (request metadata, timestamps, non-payload trace) are retained for 30 days by default; payloads are not stored by default unless you enable debug logging. We include options in the console to redact or disable trace collection.

3) Sandbox key scope:
- Yes — we create environment-scoped API keys (dev, staging, prod). I’ll provision a dev/scoped sandbox key once you confirm the primary dev user (email).

Compliance docs:
- I’ve attached our SOC 2 summary + DPA link in the console. I can also CC our security rep if you want a direct call.

Next steps (action items):
- Emily/Carlos: send the dev contact email and a small sample payload (anonymized).
- Ben: provision the dev key, apply the 14-day evaluation bump, and add the 1M token credit to the account.
- Follow-up: 30-min sync to review traffic and logs — Tue 4/14 10:30 PT suggested.

If that all works I’ll get the key and bump in place today.

Ben
